title: The cave (1 Samuel 24)
hookLine: David could kill Saul and cuts only his robe

cards: David is now a fugitive. King Saul has taken three thousand chosen men into the wild country near En-gedi, rocks so steep only wild goats climb them, to hunt him down. David and his men are hiding deep in a cave.
And of all the caves in the desert, Saul walks into theirs. Alone. He's come in, the text says politely, to ease nature.
He has no idea who is sitting a few yards behind him in the dark. David's men lean in and whisper: this is the day the Lord promised. Your enemy, delivered into your hand.

teach.b: David creeps forward in the dark, close enough to strike, and secretly cuts off the hem of Saul's robe. That's all. And then, the Douay-Rheims says, "David's heart struck him."
Even that small cut bothers his conscience. He stops his men from going any further: Saul is still, in David's words, the Lord's anointed.

teach.h: ONLY THE HEM OF HIS ROBE.
teach.b: Saul walks out of the cave and goes on his way, never knowing how close it was. Then David takes a real risk. He steps out after him and calls: My lord the king!
David bows to the ground before the man trying to kill him, holds up the piece of cloth, and calls him my father.
I had a thought to kill thee, "but my eye hath spared thee. For I said: I will not put out my hand against my lord." I will not. That's the whole story in three words.
David has a reason, an opportunity, and men cheering him on. He also has the one thing that matters more: a line he won't cross. And for a moment, it breaks Saul open.
"Is this thy voice, my son David?"

teach.h: THOU ART MORE JUST THAN I.
teach.b: Saul weeps out loud, and says: "Thou art more just than I." It doesn't last. Saul will hunt David again.
Mercy doesn't always change the other person. But it changes who David is.
Catholic readers see in this cave an early picture of what Jesus will ask: not repaying evil for evil, even when you could, even when everyone around you says you should.

how: Catholics hear David's mercy to Saul in the weekday Mass readings, and the Church reads it alongside Jesus's teaching to love one's enemies and not repay evil for evil.

games.q: you're David. the king who wants you dead is alone in your cave, a few yards away, and your men whisper that God has delivered him to you. what do you do?
o: cut the hem of his robe, and let him go.
tie him up and make him promise peace.
games.why: David cuts only the hem, and even that troubles his heart. then he calls Saul back and says: I will not put out my hand against my lord.

practice: Think of someone who has hurt you, and who, honestly, you could hurt back: a secret you know, a comment you could make, a forward button, a group chat.
Put yourself in the cave with the chance right in front of you, let it go by, and say quietly David's three words: I will not. If you pray, ask for the strength to keep that line.

wordCard.voice: The cave. Where David had his enemy alone in the dark, cut only the hem of his robe, and said I will not. Today's word.
